questions.question_english: 96. Article 129 of the Constitution designates the Supreme Court of India as a 'Court of Record'. What is a primary legal implication of this designation?
options_english: Its records and proceedings have evidentiary value and cannot be questioned when produced before any subordinate court.
Its judgments are subject to mandatory annual review by a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
It lacks the power to penalize individuals for contempt of court.
It can only adjudicate disputes between Union Cabinet Ministers.
questions.explanation_english: The correct answer is that the records and proceedings of the Supreme Court have evidentiary value and cannot be questioned when presented in any subordinate court. Under Article 129, being designated as a 'Court of Record' means that the Supreme Court's judgments, decrees, and proceedings are preserved for their evidentiary value and hold legal authority when referenced in lower courts. Additionally, this status grants the Supreme Court the inherent power to punish for contempt, thereby maintaining judicial dignity.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (a) है। अनुच्छेद 129 के तहत, सर्वोच्च न्यायालय का 'रिकॉर्ड का न्यायालय' होना इसका एक प्रमुख कानूनी परिणाम है कि इसके रिकॉर्ड और कार्यवाही का साक्ष्य मूल्य है और इसे किसी भी अधीनस्थ न्यायालय के समक्ष प्रस्तुत किए जाने पर प्रश्नित नहीं किया जा सकता। इसके निर्णय, आदेश और कार्यवाही साक्ष्य मूल्य के लिए संरक्षित होते हैं और अधीनस्थ न्यायालयों में संदर्भित किए जाने पर कानूनी अधिकार रखते हैं। इसके अलावा, इस स्थिति से सर्वोच्च न्यायालय को अवमानना के लिए दंडित करने की अंतर्निहित शक्ति भी मिलती है, जिससे न्यायिक गरिमा बनी रहती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Its records and proceedings have evidentiary value and cannot be questioned when produced before any subordinate court.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Article 129, declaring the Supreme Court a 'Court of Record' carries two primary legal consequences: First, its judgments, decrees, and proceedings are recorded for perpetual memory and evidentiary value, possessing indisputable legal authority when produced before any subordinate court.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Under Article 67(b) of the Constitution, the Vice-President of India can be removed from office by a resolution passed by an effective majority—a majority of all the then members—of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha by a simple majority.

questions.question_english: 14. Which statement accurately distinguishes the pardoning power of a State Governor under Article 161 from that of the President under Article 72?
options_english: The Governor can pardon punishment imposed by a Court Martial, whereas the President cannot.
The Governor can pardon offences under central laws, whereas the President cannot.
The Governor’s power extends to all cases involving federal tax defaults.
The Governor cannot pardon a sentence of death, whereas the President can.
questions.explanation_english: The Governor cannot pardon a sentence of death, whereas the President can. Under Article 161, a Governor can grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishment for offences against state laws. However, the Governor lacks the power to completely pardon a sentence of death, which remains exclusively within the domain of the President under Article 72. The Governor can only suspend, remit, or commute a death sentence, keeping complete clemency powers for capital punishment with the President.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (d) है। राज्यपाल मृत्युदंड की सजा को माफ नहीं कर सकता, जबकि राष्ट्रपति कर सकता है। अनुच्छेद 161 के तहत, राज्यपाल राज्य कानूनों के खिलाफ अपराधों के लिए माफी, पुनर्विचार, राहत या दंड की माफी दे सकता है। हालाँकि, राज्यपाल के पास मृत्युदंड की सजा को पूरी तरह से माफ करने का अधिकार नहीं है, जो कि राष्ट्रपति के अनुच्छेद 72 के तहत विशेष रूप से है। राज्यपाल केवल मृत्युदंड को निलंबित, माफ या परिवर्तित कर सकता है, जबकि राष्ट्रपति के पास पूरक दंड के लिए पूर्ण शक्ति होती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) The Governor cannot pardon a sentence of death, whereas the President can.
